stem: A pharmacist fills Belsomra for home use. A coworker says the transaction is not reportable because the drug is neither an opioid nor a benzodiazepine. Which response is correct?

choices.text: Agree; MassPAT is limited to those two drug classes.
Agree; insomnia drugs are Massachusetts Schedule VI.
Report it because covered Schedule IV dispensing is reportable.
Report it only after the fifth refill.
Omit it unless the prescriber requests reporting.

explanation.core_reasoning: Belsomra is Schedule IV, and the stated outpatient dispensing is covered by MassPAT. Reportability does not depend on the drug being an opioid or benzodiazepine.

choice_analysis.A: MassPAT reporting extends beyond opioids and benzodiazepines.
choice_analysis.B: Suvorexant remains Schedule IV despite its insomnia indication.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. Schedule IV status brings the covered dispensing within the reporting rule.
choice_analysis.D: Reporting occurs for each covered dispensing, not only after a refill threshold.
choice_analysis.E: Prescriber preference does not control pharmacy PMP reporting.

related_facts: Belsomra (suvorexant) is federal and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
Covered Massachusetts pharmacy dispensings of Schedule II through V drugs are reportable to MassPAT.
explanation.mpje_trap: A nonbenzodiazepine hypnotic can still be controlled and reportable.

reasoning_steps: Apply the schedule-based MassPAT reporting rule
Reject therapeutic-class exclusions not found in the reporting rule
